Thread: Today is a good day for Brexit, there's no denying that, and we Brits finally have some sort of agreement in place with the EU about something that actually matters - the rights of citizens of the EU in the UK, and vice versa. Fantastic. Genuinely brilliant news. 1/

First, May activated Article 50 without there being an established consensus in the cabinet, for what we wanted to achieve, let alone a consensus amongst the British Public. The fact that they still haven't had that chat means May is agreeing with whoever shouts the loudest. 5/

Next, May called a snap election which not only weakened her mandate (already fairly weak, truth be told), has allowed her to be held to ransom by the DUP and her own back benchers, and cost us roughly 2 months of negotating time. 6/

And yes, I think we need a new referendum, one to determine if we still want to walk this path. Let's have our chat, like adults, present all the information and allow an informed electorate to decide between proceeding with Leave, or revoking Article 50. Supermajorty wins. 11/
